content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with sauce and meat is a school‑lunch dish consisting of boiled pasta, a tomato‑based sauce, and pieces of boiled or stewed meat. The meal provides energy and nutrients needed by children for a school day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Short‑shaped pasta such as shells or penne is commonly used in school cafeterias because it holds sauce well.
The sauce is usually made from tomatoes, onion, carrot and a small amount of vegetable oil, providing vitamin C and beta‑carotene.
Meat is typically beef or chicken, cut into small pieces for easy chewing by children.
Pasta is one of the most popular items on school menus worldwide.
The dish scales easily: a single large batch can serve hundreds of students.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pasta supplies a steady release of energy, helping maintain blood‑sugar levels throughout the school day.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat in the sauce adds complete protein needed for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomato sauce provides vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, while the meat contributes iron and zinc.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Durum‑wheat pasta contains dietary fiber that promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of carbs and protein helps children feel full longer.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat pasta contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; excess sodium may be a concern for children with hypertension.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: Improperly cooked or low‑quality meat can harbor bacteria, so proper cooking temperatures are essential.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some schools use preservatives or flavor enhancers; those with sensitivities should check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The dish is served hot in portion trays. Children can use a fork or spoon, mixing the pasta with the sauce so each piece is coated. Grated cheese may be added if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared pasta with sauce and meat should be kept refrigerated at +2…+4 °C for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze in airtight containers and reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.
